newsitem.title: USA: IBM winner in Internet service survey.
newsitem.headline: IBM winner in Internet service survey.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp.'s Internet access service was the winner in a survey of 12 leading Internet service providers, PC World magazine says.
The computer giant's IBM Internet Connection service was rated A-plus in the survey of 3,800 online users, which will appear in PC World's February issue hitting newsstands Tuesday.
PC World rated IBM's service and the Mindspring service "Best Buys."
Coming in last was Netcom, which received a D-minus. Grades of D were handed out to No. 1 online service provider America Online Inc. and No. 2 CompuServe Corp.
Computer users need Internet access services to hook up to the globe-spanning Net to receive e-mail, browse Web pages, download data and software, and perform other online tasks.

Visitors to PC World Online's Web site (http://www.pcworld.com) answered questions about overall satisfaction, whether they had trouble connecting and downloading files and whether they were happy with technical support they received.
Three Internet access providers received B-plus grades: Mindspring "Best Buy," MCI Internet and Sprynet, according to PC World.
Getting a C-plus were AT&T Corp.'s AT&T Worldnet service and Earthlink Network. GTE Internet Solutions received a C, while Concentric Network and Microsoft Corp.'s Microsoft Network got a C-minus.
Respondents surveyed via PC World Online's Web site also reviewed smaller, regional service providers.

Before signing up for an Internet service, PC World recommends asking whether the service offers a flat rate for unlimited access -- $19.95 a month is the rate most frequently charged -- and whether there is a start-up fee, free trial period and local access phone number.

The magazine also urged prospective customers to find out if the service has a toll-free number for access away from home, whether it provides toll-free technical advice and if they can publish personal Web pages via the service.
IBM Internet Connection (800 455-5056; http://www.ibm.net) is available for computers running on all Windows operating systems, IBM's OS/2 operating system and Macintosh operating systems.
Mindspring (800 719-4332, http://www.mindspring.com) runs on Windows, OS/2 and Mac systems.
